beats.care: It tests a right you have: peaceful protest. Police can still detain people in advance if they fear trouble.
beats.what: A Special Executive Magistrate in Delhi released CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday on conditional bail. Student leader Neha Bora was released earlier that morning.
beats.why: Police held them on Friday under preventive sections of the BNSS before a planned march, saying they wanted to stop a breach of peace.

cards.body: Most were held around Connaught Place on Friday evening, where the Cockroach Janta Party had called supporters to gather.
cards.caption: People detained, police said

cards.body: It is a written promise to a magistrate to keep the peace and behave well for a set time. Breaking it can mean arrest or paying money.
cards.title: what's a peace bond?

cards.body: Earlier this week, two CJP spokespersons were sent to jail for five days for climbing barricades at Jantar Mantar, and asked for one-year good-behaviour bonds.

a.body: The arrests were unlawful and meant to stop a peaceful march before it even began.
a.label: CJP says

b.body: Preventive detention was needed to stop a breach of peace and protect traffic and order.
b.label: Delhi Police says

cards.title: Was holding them in advance fair?

cards.q: Should police be allowed to detain protest leaders before a march?

opts: Holding someone to stop a possible offence
cards.why: Police held Dipke and Bora before the march, to prevent a feared breach of peace, not for a crime already proven.

cover.label: People police say were detained before Friday's march

hook: Detained before a march, freed a day later. What does a *peace bond* actually ask of you?

learn.t: BNSS Section 170 lets police arrest someone to prevent a crime, without a warrant or a magistrate's order.

effects.label: Asked to sign a peace bond
